Do I need to write any code?
No. You make a bot in Telegram, paste a token, and put your Joinvoo link in your ads. Most people are live in about 10 minutes.
How are deposits matched to my ads?

Your broker, casino, affiliate network or bot sends a small postback when someone deposits. Joinvoo matches it to the person who joined and the ad they came from, and sends Purchase with the value to your ad platform. You can also mark a deposit by hand.
Can I keep my own bot, landing page and domain?
Yes. Track your own bot’s Start without sharing its token, keep your landing page with one line of code, and run links on your own domain. Request-to-join channels are supported.
Yes. Joinvoo only uses Telegram’s official Bot API, the same invite-link features any channel admin can use. Your bot never posts in your channel.
What happens when my credits run out?
Your ads keep working and people still get into your channel. Tracking pauses until you top up, and you’ll see a banner in your dashboard.

You need two things from Events Manager:
Open Events Manager and choose your dataset (pixel) on the left. If you don’t have one, tap Connect data → Web to create it.
Copy the Dataset ID (also called Pixel ID). It’s a long number like 884210395527140.
Open the Settings tab, scroll to Conversions API, and tap Generate access token. Copy the long token.
In Joinvoo, paste both and tap Save and send a test.

To watch the test arrive, open the Test events tab in Events Manager, copy the code shown there (like TEST12345), and paste it into Joinvoo’s Test code box before sending. Clear the test code when you go live, or real joins only show up in the test tab.

In TikTok Ads Manager go to Tools → Events → Web events, open your pixel, copy the Pixel code (letters and numbers, like CABC123DEF456GHI), then in its Settings tap Generate access token. Paste both into Joinvoo’s TikTok tab and send a test.
In Snapchat Ads Manager, open Events Manager and select your Snap Pixel (create one if you don’t have it). Copy the Pixel ID. It looks like a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab.
Generate a Conversions API token. You’ll find it in Business settings or in the pixel’s setup in Events Manager. Copy it.
Paste both into Joinvoo’s Snapchat tab and tap Send test. The test goes to Snapchat’s validation endpoint, so it checks your ID and token without adding a real event.

If your channel or bot sends people to a broker, casino, shop or app, you can send their sign-ups, first deposits, repeat deposits and sales back to your ad platforms too. Your ads then learn to find depositors, not just joiners. These events cost nothing extra.
In your dashboard, open Conversions and copy your postback URL. It’s unique to your account and looks like this:

Pass the Telegram ID to your offer. Your bot knows the Telegram ID of everyone who presses Start. Add it to the offer link the bot sends as sub1, for example https://offer.example.com/?sub1=7012345678. Most networks and trackers call this a sub ID or click ID.

Paste the postback URL into your affiliate network, Keitaro, Binom, CRM or broker as the postback for registrations and deposits. Swap the placeholders for that tool’s own macros: its sub1 macro for {telegram_id}, its payout or amount macro for {payout}, and its transaction ID macro for {transaction_id}.

Set status to the event: lead, reg (sign-up), ftd (first deposit), dep (repeat deposit), sale (course, VIP, subscription), qualified (CPA qualified) or rejected (chargeback or reversal: removes the revenue and sends nothing to ad platforms). Later deposits from the same person are recorded as repeat deposits automatically.

Macro names differ between tools; check your network’s postback help page. Joinvoo also accepts subid, aff_sub or tg_id for the Telegram ID; event or goal for the status; value or amount for the payout.
No postback? Open a person’s profile in People and tap Mark as deposited. Joinvoo sends the deposit to your ad platforms just the same.
To optimise for depositors, pick Purchase (Meta), CompletePayment (TikTok) or PURCHASE (Snapchat) as the conversion event in your ad set once deposits start coming in.

My channel didn’t appear after I added the bot

Make sure you added the bot as an admin, not just a member, and that Invite users via link is on. Then run setup again from the Help tab, and on the channel step tap The bot was already an admin?. Pick your bot and type your channel’s @username (or its ID for a private channel).
Someone removed the bot’s admin rights or switched off Invite users via link. In Telegram: open your channel → Administrators → your bot → switch it back on. Joinvoo picks it up by itself.
Most of my joins show as “Organic”

Those people joined without going through your tracking link: from search (public channels), a link someone shared, or an old invite link in your ad. Check that every ad uses the Joinvoo tracking link, and make the channel private if you can.
My ad platform shows fewer events than Joinvoo

That’s normal. Meta, TikTok and Snapchat only count events they can match to one of their users, and they remove duplicates. Events can also take up to 20 minutes to appear. If a join shows failed, tap it to see the platform’s reason.

Generate a new access token in your ad platform (for Meta: Events Manager → Settings → Conversions API) and paste it on the Channels page. Joins that failed are retried for a while, so recent ones still get sent.

Joinvoo needs the person’s Telegram ID in sub1 (or subid, aff_sub, tg_id). Check that your bot adds it to the offer link and that your network sends it back in the postback. Placeholders that weren’t filled in, like {sub1}, are ignored.

Telegram limits how fast one bot can make links. For big campaigns, add a second or third bot to the same channel (make each one admin). Joinvoo uses all of them. If links ever run out, visitors still get in through a backup link; only those joins aren’t matched.
